display.title: The Mysterious Broom Maker
display.summary_short: When a cruel poritz threatens to expel the Jews of Kobrin, Reb Leib Sarah's sends their leader to spend Shabbos with a poor broom maker deep in the forest.
display.summary_long: The storyteller introduces Reb Leib Sarah's, born through the Baal Shem Tov's blessing, who traveled far and wide on missions to help Jews. In the Berditchev marketplace, Reb Binyomin, leader of the nearby town of Kobrin, begs for help: the new poritz demands years of back rent his kind father never asked for, and threatens to throw the Jews out and take everything. Reb Leib visits the poritz, who offers to cancel the debt if the Jews secretly join a Polish uprising against the Czar. Reb Leib refuses, because the Torah teaches loyalty to the government of the land. Then comes "plan B": Reb Binyomin must bring food for Shabbos to a poor broom maker named Yaakov, deep in the forest, and tell no one. That night he hears heavenly singing and sees a blinding light in the hut, and he realizes Yaakov is one of the hidden tzaddikim. After Havdalah Yaakov tells him the decree is gone. At home he learns that Cossacks arrested the poritz on Shabbos morning. Months later the governor explains why and gives the Jews the land as a gift from the Czar, but no one may know the part the broom maker played.
display.lesson: Trust in Hashem and stay loyal to the government of the land; Hashem has hidden tzaddikim in every generation through whom He saves His people.

advisories.note: A hostile poritz threatens to expel the Jews of a town and seize their belongings; resolved happily.
